in.rationale: Michael et al. note inductive or tacit knowledge may not admit short justifications and that alternative extraction methods may be needed. out.rationale: Saunders et al. state critique-based assistance does not address problems a model cannot put into words and that the critique-discrimination gap may stay large. Michael et al. ask whether debate can extract inductive or tacit knowledge lacking short citeable justifications, noting debaters revealed only about 3.5% of the story on average; one concerns critiques of summaries, the other debate on reading comprehension.
out.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: whether oversight methods can surface model knowledge that the model cannot express as short, checkable statements

state_meaning: AI-drafted candidate; no person has reviewed it.
text: The authors note that in their debates debaters justify positions with a few claims grounded in textual evidence and reveal only about 3.5% of the story on average, but knowledge such as complex patterns induced from many examples, expert intuition, linguistic knowledge or task know-how may not admit such simple explanations, or debaters may not know how to justify it succinctly. They state that testing debate on questions about such knowledge, or designing alternative extraction methods, may be needed to know whether it can be reliably extracted from AI systems.
title: Can debate extract inductive or tacit knowledge that lacks short, citeable justifications?
